name: Dry pho
summary: Two bowls at breakfast. One holds sun-dried rice noodles tossed with meat and fermented black soybean sauce. The other holds a clear bone broth. Go Vietnam puts the shops around Kon Tum market from about 6:00 to 10:00.
origin: Go Vietnam calls dry phở the breakfast of Kon Tum city, carried over from Gia Lai’s two-bowl service.
history: Go Vietnam traces the dried noodle to Pleiku. It credits a first highland workshop to Hầu Tắc Cái and Hứa Thị Thủy on Bà Triệu, and the two-bowl nickname to Nguyễn Thành Mỹ’s Đại Hưng restaurant on Hoàng Diệu around 1959, where one order of dry chicken phở arrived as two bowls. From Gia Lai it spread to Kon Tum. The same article says the dish was recognized for Asian culinary value in 2012.
taste: Go Vietnam describes the dry bowl as salty-sweet black sauce with the fat of the meat, peanuts, and crispy pork or fried shallots. The broth is clear and sweet from bones, without the cinnamon, star anise, and cardamom of northern phở. Lime and chili are the sour-spicy lift.
howToEat: Toss the dry bowl with the black sauce and toppings. Season with lime, chili, or fish sauce. Eat a bite of noodles, then sip the hot broth. Go Vietnam says many people add blanched bean sprouts and raw herbs to the dry bowl. Eat it hot, in the morning, before the noodles cool.

The chicken bowl uses shredded or sliced chicken. The beef bowl uses thin beef, sometimes with small minced-beef balls. Beef broth is pork and beef bones. Chicken broth is pork and chicken bones. Herbs served aside are bean sprouts, lettuce, basil, and coriander.
where: Around Kon Tum market and the central streets. Go Vietnam names Phan Chu Trinh, Phan Đình Phùng, and Tô Hiến Thành among the morning streets. Shop hours on that article are mainly about 6:00 to 10:00.
priceBand: Go Vietnam prints about 20,000–33,000 VND a bowl, and up to 35,000 VND for a large bowl, as a 2025 reference.
seoTitle: Dry pho in Kon Tum — two bowls at the market
seoDescription: Sun-dried noodles with black soybean sauce in one bowl and clear broth in the other, around the market from about 6:00 to 10:00. Go Vietnam prints about 20,000–33,000 VND.
